review_notes: Read the whole target file and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean. I compared `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` with `Module.Basis.baseChange` and `Module.Free.tensor`. I grepped for uses: `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` is used directly in Trace.lean and in this file, and `Basis.baseChange` in Kaehler/Cotangent files. I did not check whether `Free.lean` transitively imports `TensorProduct/Basis.lean`; it probably does via Matrix.ToLin, but I did not confirm it. I did not check whether the two bases are definitionally equal, so a migration may need a bridging lemma. The `toMatrix_baseChange` lemma and the `baseChange_linearMap`/`baseChange_end` lemmas are useful API and are not flagged as duplicates. They would have to be restated for the surviving basis.

findings.declaration: Algebra.TensorProduct.basis (with basisAux, basisAux_tmul, basisAux_map_smul, basis_repr_tmul, basis_apply, basis_repr_symm_apply, basis_repr_symm_apply')
findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def basis : Basis ι A (A ⊗[R] M) where
  repr := { basisAux A b with map_smul' := basisAux_map_smul b }
findings.problem: This file builds the A-basis of `A ⊗[R] M` induced by an R-basis of `M` from scratch. Mathlib already has `Module.Basis.baseChange`, which builds the same basis under the same hypotheses: `S` a `Semiring` with an `R`-algebra structure, and `b : Basis ι R M`. It comes with the same simp API: `baseChange_apply : b.baseChange S i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i` and `baseChange_repr_tmul`. The two bases therefore have separate constructions, separate `basis_apply`/`baseChange_apply` lemmas and separate repr lemmas. Downstream files use both: Trace.lean uses `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`, while the Kaehler and Cotangent files use `Basis.baseChange`. Even this file shows the clash: it adds `Module.Basis.baseChange_linearMap` and `Module.Basis.baseChange_end` in the `Basis.baseChange` namespace, but states them for `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`.
findings.proposed_change: Make one construction canonical. The simplest option is to define `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A b` as `b.baseChange A`, or deprecate it. Then derive `basis_repr_tmul`, `basis_apply` and `basis_repr_symm_apply'` from `Basis.baseChange_repr_tmul` and `Basis.baseChange_apply`, or drop them. Delete `basisAux` and its two lemmas. State `toMatrix_baseChange`, `Basis.baseChange_linearMap` and `Basis.baseChange_end` with `b.baseChange A`. Keep `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` as an abbreviation or deprecated alias only if the name is wanted. The reverse direction also works: make `Basis.baseChange` the thin wrapper over this construction, if that is preferred.
findings.benefit: There is one basis of the base change with one set of simp lemmas, so users no longer need to convert between `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A b` and `b.baseChange A`. Simp sets are no longer split between two equal bases, and about 40 lines of duplicated construction and proof go away.

evidence.excerpt:
def baseChange (b : Basis ι R M) : Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M) :=
  (tensorProduct (.singleton Unit S) b).reindex (Equiv.punitProd ι)
(b.baseChange S).repr (x ⊗ₜ y) i = b.repr y i • x

findings.excerpt:
instance instFree (R A M : Type*)
    [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] :
    Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M) :=
findings.problem: This instance is a second route to the same fact as Mathlib's `Module.Free.tensor`. `Module.Free.tensor` gives `Module.Free S (M ⊗[R] N)` from `Module.Free S M` and `Module.Free R N`. Taking `M := A` and `N := M` gives the same statement, because `Module.Free A A` is available as an instance. Instance resolution therefore has two ways to find the same class instance. This is the weakest part of the finding: the two are not literally the same declaration, and this one is proved from the competing basis.
findings.proposed_change: Either remove `instFree`, since `Module.Free.tensor` should already apply, or keep it and prove it with `Module.Free.of_basis (Module.Basis.baseChange A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M))`. Check which instance is actually found before deleting. If it is kept, say in the docstring why it is kept.
findings.benefit: This avoids two competing instances and proofs of the same class, and removes the last dependence of the instance on the file's own basis construction.
